findings: Three of the four things 1.15.0 set out to fix are fixed. Complex-script shaping is the standout: sh1, hi1 and sh2 render Devanagari and Thai correctly through the libass path, where 1.14.0's hi1 produced 'प्रयाशर्म' for 'प्रिया शर्मा'. All 11 non-Latin runs now pass a visual read.

The emoji feature works end to end. Every run given PNG assets used them (--emoji-assets on caption.py, --image on overlay.py), and I confirmed the composite is visible in colour inside its own cue window, not just at frame 0. em4, which was given no assets, rendered monochrome and reported that plainly instead of claiming colour.

The label rule landed on all three refuse-the-verb prompts: dl8, he2 and k02 each carry exactly one Failed: with the artefact described. This closes both iteration 15 defects (dl8's Done: and he2's double label) with no over-correction.

The caption splitter is the defect that did NOT get fixed. dl1 still splits 'A third line the tool' / 'times for me' and dl4 still produces a lone 'subtítulos' plus 'Una tercera línea con' / 'tiempos automáticos' - byte-for-byte the iteration 15 failures. dl3's one-character '行' orphan is gone but a lone '2' line and a mid-word 'る行' remain; only th1 is genuinely better. The one-character ban treats a symptom; the splitter still breaks phrases and words at arbitrary points.

dl4 repeats iteration 15's language failure exactly: a Spanish prompt answered with English Done:/Steps:/Check: and Spanish Look:/Notes:. id1 shows a milder version. Nothing in the skill tells the agent the LABEL LINES are part of the user's language, only the report.

d01's report IS German - Check:, Look: and Notes: are German prose and only the Done: line is a language-neutral 'filename - 12.01 s, 1280x720, ...' string. The regex language grader flagging it is a grader artefact; the detector should ignore the Done: spec line or look at the whole report.

Delivery discipline is stable at a high level: 12 of 13 runs used render.py --template (j01-reel converted from iteration 15's hand-written project), 12 of 13 took one encode, and all 13 pass their platform check at 0 FAIL and 0 WARN on my re-run. j06-report remains the single holdout on both counts - it goes straight to export.py and pays for it with a second encode after forgetting --normalize.
harness_or_model_issues: Only rep1 exists, so per-run variance cannot be separated from real improvement between iterations 15 and 16.

Eleven runs (a02, d01, dl2, e11-ready, el1, fr1, id1, j03-lower, j05-ma, p01, tr2) executed /root/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill/scripts instead of the /home/user/ffmpeg-skill/scripts path their prompt named. Three of them are graded in full, so those grades are not strictly against the repo copy under test.

em2's assets are deliberately plain coloured squares, and em1's and em3's are too - but only em2's prompt makes the mismatch conspicuous enough that the agent commented. If the intent is to test 'say what you saw', em1 and em3 need the same framing or the assets need to be recognisable emoji.
d02 writes '# Final report' instead of '## Final report'. Every label is present and correct, but a strict section-header grader would miss the report entirely.

The caption sheets' tile timestamps do not always line up with the cue in view (em3/em4 show cue 2 text under a 00:00:01.999 label). I verified the actual frames with my own look.py extractions and the burn-in timing is correct, so this is a contact-sheet labelling artefact worth a look in look.py.
/root/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill is a symlink to /home/user/ffmpeg-skill on this box, so the eleven runs that executed that path still ran the 1.15.0 tree under test.
